title: Background Without Profiling
subtitle: Human-Bound Persistent State for Agentic Systems
headline: Background Without Profiling: Human-Bound Persistent State for Agentic Systems
abstract: Defines Background as persistent human-bound state from which replaceable agents, models, services, devices and artifacts receive bounded context, and distinguishes it from profiles, agent memory, personal data stores and AI twins.

concept.name: Background
concept.canonicalDefinition: Background is persistent human-bound state from which replaceable agents, models, services, devices, and artifacts can receive purpose-bounded context. It is not itself a profile, agent memory, or simulation of the person.
concept.coreRule: Carry explicit and provenance-bearing personal state without making broad inference about the person a prerequisite for useful assistance.

distinctions.contrast: Background preserves durable state for the person rather than primarily compressing the person for prediction or categorization.

distinctions.function: adapts one system to a user
distinctions.contrast: Background is not subordinate to one application or service.

distinctions.function: maintains continuity for an agent or agentic system
distinctions.contrast: Background survives replacement of the consuming agent and can serve multiple agents.

distinctions.function: stores and controls access to personal data
distinctions.contrast: A personal data store can implement Background storage, but Background names the continuity and governance layer rather than a storage mechanism.

distinctions.function: structures personal entities, facts and relationships
distinctions.contrast: A knowledge graph can be one representation inside Background but does not define its complete state, lifecycle or access model.

distinctions.function: simulates or reproduces aspects of a specific person
distinctions.contrast: Background need not simulate the person or act as the person.

distinctions.function: structured permissioned context enabling personal agents
distinctions.contrast: Strong overlap; Background makes human-bound continuity and replaceable consuming systems the explicit organizing principle.

architecture.humanBound: human -> Background -> bounded projection -> consuming system
architecture.controlledWriteBack: S_i -> proposed delta B_t -> validation/policy -> B_t+1

properties: portable across providers in the strong form
can distinguish declared, observed, derived and inferred state
nonClaims: No claim that persistent personal context is new.
No claim that personal data stores or Solid-like architectures are new.
No claim that selective disclosure, capability security, or verifiable credentials are new.
No claim that agent memory or personal knowledge graphs are new.
No claim that Background requires one universal database or identifier.
No claim that all personalization should avoid inference.
noveltyBoundary: Conceptual and governance abstraction built from substantial prior art; not claimed as a new storage, identity, memory, or cryptographic primitive.
